Metadata.description: A student project, not for real borrowers. Some rates come from unofficial sources and may be old or wrong.

Home.title: Vay Đúng
Home.tagline: Vay Đúng helps you estimate the real cost of a loan, check a lender, and know when not to borrow.

points.cost: Estimates the real yearly rate, including monthly fees and mandatory insurance with a known amount, so you can compare loans.
points.licensed: Compares only products from institutions on the State Bank of Vietnam's list, with the source and the date checked. Being on the list doesn't mean the State Bank recommends that product, or that the loan is right for you. Some rates come from unofficial sources.
points.honest: Tells you plainly when an amount goes over the Vay Đúng guideline for what you can repay, and suggests other options.
points.independent: Currently takes no money from lenders, doesn't sell your information, and doesn't lend.

Home.privacy: No login. What you enter in the questionnaire and lender check is calculated only on your device and isn't sent anywhere. See Privacy at the bottom of the page.
Home.headline: Before you borrow, know what you'll really have to pay
Home.exampleTitle: Why the advertised number isn't enough
Home.exampleBody: For example: borrowing {amount} over {term} months at a flat 1.5% a month. It sounds like 18% a year, but because interest is charged on the original amount for the whole term, you repay {total} in total. On a reducing-balance basis, that's equivalent to about {apr} a year.

This could fit with some options, but it isn't certain: the rate you're approved for, unknown fees or the product's own conditions could push it over. Ask for the exact monthly payment before you sign.

too_much.body: Under the Vay Đúng guideline, total debt payments shouldn't exceed {limit} of your income each month. For you that's {max}. You already pay {debt}, leaving only {headroom} for a new loan. The principal alone would be about {principalOnly} a month, before interest.

too_much_with_interest.body: Under the Vay Đúng guideline, total debt payments shouldn't exceed {limit} of your income each month. For you that's {max}. You already pay {debt}, leaving only {headroom} for a new loan. Even at the lowest rate we found, this loan needs about {lowestPayment} a month.

no_income.title: We don't recommend borrowing without a regular income
no_income.body: A loan has to be repaid every month, even before you find work. Paying late adds more interest and can damage your credit history.

no_data.body: Under the Vay Đúng guideline, total debt payments shouldn't exceed {limit} of your income each month. For you that's {max}. You already pay {debt}, leaving {headroom} for a new loan. The principal alone is about {principalOnly} a month, before interest and fees, so the real payment will be higher. If the monthly payment is above {headroom}, we don't recommend borrowing this amount. Ask for the exact monthly payment before you sign.

Alternatives.title: What you could do instead
Alternatives.smaller: Borrow less: about {amount} over {term} months could fit (estimate at {lender}'s highest rate).
Alternatives.longer: Repay over a longer time: the monthly payment falls, but the total cost rises.
Alternatives.payDebt: Pay down your current debts before borrowing more.
Alternatives.save: Save part of it first, then borrow less or not at all.
Alternatives.family: Ask family, or ask your employer about a salary advance.
Alternatives.avoid: Don't turn to loan sharks or loan apps of unknown origin. If you're asked to transfer money before receiving a loan, stop and check with the lender's official hotline.
Alternatives.familyNoIncome: Ask family whether they can help for now.

Guidance.title: What to know for this need
Guidance.phone: Buying electronics: ask about installments at the store first. If a plan is advertised as 0%, ask whether any fees or insurance come with it. If none do, it can be cheaper than a cash loan. Compare the total you'd pay.
Guidance.motorbike: Buying a motorbike: compare dealer installments with a cash loan. Some installment loans use the bike as security or set conditions on its registration papers, so ask before signing. The total you'd pay is the number to compare.
Guidance.education: Tuition: first ask about scholarships and paying in stages. If you're a student in difficult circumstances, ask your school or the Vietnam Bank for Social Policies about its student loan programme and whether you qualify.
Guidance.medical: An emergency: check your health insurance and ask family first. If you still need to borrow, use only a lender on the State Bank of Vietnam's list, even in a hurry.
Guidance.debt: Borrowing to pay debt: be careful, debts can snowball. First ask your current lender about more time or a new repayment schedule. Only take a new loan if its real cost is clearly lower than the old one.
Guidance.living: Borrowing for everyday spending: the loan raises your monthly payments while your income stays the same. See whether you can cut spending or get a salary advance first.
Guidance.other: A cash loan is flexible but can be expensive. If you still borrow, borrow only what you need, and compare the total you'd pay before you choose.
Guidance.urgent: In a hurry: people who need money fast are easier to scam. Be wary if anyone makes you transfer money first, especially to a personal account, before approving or paying out a loan. Don't rely on a contract sent by message, because contracts can be forged too. Call the lender's official hotline before transferring anything.
Guidance.goods: Buying on instalments: ask the shop for the cash price and the instalment price and compare them, as the loan usually goes straight to the shop, not to you. If it isn't urgent, saving up first is usually cheaper.

Results.why1: We put loans you can afford first, then those with a lower real rate, calculated at the highest known rate, because nobody knows yet which rate you'd get. The figure includes monthly fees and mandatory insurance with a known amount, but not insurance that's optional or may not be mandatory. This order isn't advice to choose any lender.
Results.why2: A product whose fees are all unknown can't be first, because its real cost may be higher than we can calculate.
Results.why3: No lender pays to be ranked higher. Vay Đúng currently takes no money from lenders, including commission, and doesn't sell your information.

The official rate and fees are those in your contract. Read it carefully before signing.

exclude.secondary_sources: We only found figures in general articles, not on an official product page or contract.
exclude.lender_unverified: We haven't been able to verify the lender named in this product's contract.
exclude.unverified: We haven't been able to verify this product and its terms on an official page. It may have changed or no longer exist.
exclude.rate_varies: The rate varies widely by programme or the source is old, so we can't work out a rate for you.
exclude.conflicting_sources: The lender's official documents give different rates or calculation methods, so we don't know which applies to you.
exclude.undated_document: The figures come from a single undated document. The bank says its rates have changed but hasn't published the new ones.
exclude.manual_check_pending: We are checking this lender's figures by hand against its public documents, so it isn't compared yet. Your actual rate depends on their assessment.
exclude.same_loan_other_channel: This looks like the same loan as this lender's cash loan through a different channel, so it isn't ranked separately.
exclude.range_basis_unknown: The bank publishes a rate range but doesn't say whether it applies to the original amount or the reducing balance, so we can't work out the cost.
exclude.floor_and_range: We only found an advertised rate ("from...") and a general range published by the company. Your actual rate depends on their assessment.
exclude.ceiling_only: We only found a general rate range, not the actual rate.
exclude.floor_only: We only found a starting rate ("from..."), not the actual range.
exclude.no_rate: We haven't found a published rate for this product.
exclude.revolving: Overdrafts and buy-now-pay-later have no fixed monthly schedule, so the same calculation can't compare them with instalment loans.

Safety.title: Check a lender
Safety.intro: Enter a lender, app or website. We compare it with the State Bank of Vietnam's lists and help you spot signs worth checking.
Safety.privacy: The check runs on your device. We don't send or keep what you enter.
Safety.nameHint: For example: a company name, app name or web address. Don't know the name? Just choose the signs below.
Safety.signsLabel: Have they done any of these?
Safety.signsHint: Optional. Choose whatever applies to you.
Safety.errorEmpty: Please enter a name or choose at least one sign.
Safety.asOf: According to the State Bank of Vietnam's list, as of {date}.
Safety.seeOnList: See the State Bank of Vietnam's list

licensed.title: This name matches an institution on the State Bank of Vietnam's list
licensed.websiteMatch: The address you entered matches this lender's website in our data.
licensed.caution: Compare the full name above with the name in the contract. This result is only about the name: it doesn't mean whoever is contacting you really is this institution, or that the loan is safe or right for you. Scammers can impersonate real lenders, so find the official website or hotline yourself to check.

similar.title: This name resembles one on the State Bank of Vietnam's list, but doesn't match
similar.body: "{name}" doesn't match any name in our data. You may have mistyped it, it may be an unrelated organisation, or someone may be using a similar name. We're drawing no conclusion about it. Did you mean:
similar.advice: Don't rely on links or phone numbers they send you. Find that lender's official website or hotline yourself and ask.

notFound.title: We didn't find this name in the data we took from the State Bank of Vietnam (as of {date})
notFound.body: We couldn't verify this name. That doesn't mean they're unlicensed or a scam: an app may have a different name from the lending company, and our data doesn't cover every type of institution (see the note below).
notFound.advice: Ask for the company's full name as written in the contract, then check again. If they won't say or have no company name, don't transfer money or send documents.

flag.generic_name: This name contains a general lending phrase, so it isn't enough to tell which company is lending. Ask for the lender's full name.
flag.too_easy: This name uses wording about easy or fast loans. It's something to check, not a conclusion.

stop.title: Stop before you transfer money or send information
stop.body: You chose signs that appear in warnings about loan scams. We can't conclude this is a scam, but don't transfer money or send more information until you've checked, even if they use a real lender's name.

Safety.signsIntro: These are signs to check, taken from warnings reported in the press.

sign.pay_first: Made me make a transfer first (file fee, insurance fee, disbursement fee, deposit…) before I'd get the loan
sign.unlock_fee: Said my file or account number was wrong, then wanted more money to fix or "unlock" it
sign.prove_finance: Made me transfer money to "prove my finances"
sign.otp: Asked for my OTP code, password or PIN
sign.personal_account: Made me transfer money to a person's personal account
sign.contacts: The app won't lend unless I allow access to my contacts, photo library or social media accounts
sign.harassment: Threatened me, or called and messaged my family or colleagues about a debt
sign.hold_id: Wanted personal photos or a relative's phone number as security for the loan
sign.short_term: Lends only for days or a few weeks, and I get less than the approved amount
sign.chat_only: Only contacts me through Zalo or Facebook, or sent a strange link to install an app
sign.no_company: No clear company name, address or contract template

why.pay_first: Hanoi police warn that being told to pay a fee before you get the loan may be a scam. Some licensed lenders do collect insurance at disbursement, so ask the official hotline before transferring anything. Don't rely on a contract sent by message, because contracts can be forged too.
why.unlock_fee: After the first fee, they often give a new reason to ask for more, then disappear.
why.prove_finance: This is one of the ways of asking for money named in warnings about fake loan apps.
why.otp: With your OTP or password, someone else can take money from your account. Don't give it to anyone.
why.personal_account: Money sent to a stranger's personal account may be hard to get back. Ask the lender's official hotline.
why.contacts: Police warn that some apps may take your relatives' numbers to pressure you if you pay late.
why.harassment: Police warn that loan sharks often collect debts this way. This sign alone doesn't show who is doing it, so keep the evidence.
why.hold_id: Hanoi police advise against putting personal information and photos on websites. Don't give these to anyone you can't verify.
why.short_term: When fees are taken as you receive the money and the term is very short, the real cost can be far higher than the approved amount suggests. Ask how much you'll receive, how much you'll repay, and when.
why.chat_only: Scammers can set up fake accounts and pages. Find the official channel yourself, and install apps only from official stores.
why.no_company: If you don't know which company is lending, you can't check its licence.

todo.title: What you should do
todo.official: Find the lender's official website or hotline yourself. Don't use links or phone numbers in messages they send, and don't click ads in search results.
todo.noPayment: Before transferring anything, ask the official hotline whether the payment is genuine.
todo.noOtp: Don't give your OTP, password or PIN to anyone.
todo.apps: Install apps only from the App Store or Google Play, and check the developer's name. Being in these stores doesn't prove an app is genuine.

paid.title: If you've transferred money and suspect a scam
paid.stop: Stop contact. Don't send more money to "get your money back".
paid.evidence: Keep the messages, transfer receipts, app name and screenshots.
paid.police: Take this evidence to your nearest police station to report it.

harassment.title: If you're being threatened over a debt
harassment.body: Stay calm and save messages and screenshots. If your phone can record, record your own calls as evidence. Ask your family to save what they receive too. Report it to your nearest police station.

Safety.disclaimer: This is information for reference, not a legal conclusion about any company, and it doesn't tell you whether a loan is safe. Our data covers only commercial banks, joint-venture banks, wholly foreign-owned banks and finance companies, taken from the State Bank of Vietnam's lists as of {date}; things may have changed since then. We haven't included foreign bank branches, the Vietnam Bank for Social Policies, the Co-operative Bank, leasing companies, microfinance institutions or people's credit funds. Brand names and websites were checked by us and don't come from the list.

who.title: Who runs this site
who.body: Vay Đúng is run by {name}. Contact: {email}.

device.title: What you enter in the questionnaire and lender check
device.body: Your income, debts, age, the amount you need, lender names and the signs you choose are processed only on your device. We don't send them anywhere or store them on a server, and there's no login.
device.language: If you switch language midway through the questionnaire, your answers are kept briefly in this browser. After 2 minutes they're no longer used, and they're deleted when you open another Vay Đúng page or close the tab.

analytics.title: No analytics tool
analytics.body: We don't currently use a visitor analytics tool. Vercel's servers still receive and log requests when you open a page, as described under Website hosting below. If we start using an analytics tool, we'll update this page first.

hosting.title: Website hosting
hosting.body: The site is hosted on Vercel, a US company, on servers outside Vietnam. When you open a page, Vercel's servers receive and log your IP address and technical request details, including the address of the page, to run and protect the service. What you enter in the questionnaire and lender check isn't part of these requests.

waitlist.title: News list
waitlist.off: The news list isn't open yet, so we aren't collecting emails right now.
waitlist.on: If you sign up, we keep only your email, when you consented, the version of the consent text, the page's language and the signup page, to tell you when Vay Đúng officially launches. We delete your email once we've told you, within {months} months at most.
waitlist.processor: Emails pass through Vercel's servers in Singapore and are stored at Supabase in its Singapore region. All of this is outside Vietnam.

rights.title: Your rights
rights.body: You have the right to know how your data is processed, to see, correct or delete it, to withdraw consent, to ask us to limit processing, to object to it, and to complain and claim compensation as the law provides. Send requests to {email}.

never.title: What we don't do
never.body: We don't sell your data, don't pass your information to lenders, and currently take no money from lenders.

email.title: When you email us
email.body: If you email us, your message is stored at Google's Gmail (a US service) so we can reply.

Banner.text: This is a student project, not meant for real borrowers and not connected to any lender. Some rates come from comparison sites, distribution partners or the press and may be old or wrong. Don't use this site to decide on a loan.

Ranking.title: How we rank loans
Ranking.intro: This page sets out each step: what we filter, what we calculate, the order we use, and how each thing you enter is used.
Ranking.tryIt: Try it with your own details

steps.title: Four steps
steps.filter: Filter: remove loans tied to goods other than your purpose; these don't appear on the results page, but they are on the Data page. Also remove, with the reason, loans where your amount, term, age or income is outside the known limits. If a limit is unknown, the loan stays and its card says so. Amounts over 100 million at finance companies are also removed: that's Vay Đúng's own rule while we await legal confirmation. Loans we can't cost, including those not re-checked for over 90 days, are listed separately with the reason.
steps.cost: Calculate: for each remaining loan, work out the monthly payment, total repaid and real rate, at the lowest and highest known rate.
steps.verdict: Conclude: say whether this amount is affordable for you, even when the answer is not to borrow. If you have no income, or the principal alone is over the guideline, we don't recommend borrowing. The same applies if every loan using the lender's own figures is over the guideline even at its lowest rate, whatever other sources say. For this we don't count loans where only the lowest rate is known, or those only for some people. If none are left, we go by other sources, and then the best conclusion is "it depends". An "affordable" conclusion needs at least one loan that fits at its highest rate, uses the lender's figure for that product or its company-wide ceiling, has fee information and age limits, has a maximum that isn't just a reference figure, and isn't reserved for existing customers or certain employers.

order.title: The order of priorities
order.intro: Each criterion only matters when loans tie on the one before it.
order.fit: Affordability: loans you can afford even at the highest rate come first, then those affordable only at a low rate, then those over the guideline.
order.proof: Documents: if you choose cash salary or no proof yet, loans asking for income papers come later. Loans whose documents are unknown aren't moved down.
order.floor: Completeness of the data: loans with a known highest rate come before those where only the lowest is known. Otherwise a "from X%" figure would win just by not telling you the rest.
order.cost: Real cost: a lower real rate comes first, compared at the highest rate, then the lowest. We use the highest because nobody knows yet which rate you'd get, and that's the risk you carry.
order.tie: Source: on an exact tie, the lender's own figure comes first.
order.feesRule: One more rule: in the default order, if the first loan's fees are all unknown and its affordability group has a loan with known fees, the cheapest of those goes first, since the other's real cost could be above the calculated figure.
order.otherSorts: You can change the order on the results page: lowest monthly payment, or lowest total cost, both at the highest known rate. Then only that number decides. You can also hide products that use sources other than the lender. Loans where only the lowest rate is known always come last, because their figure is only a minimum.
order.conditions: Conditions we don't ask about: a loan only for existing customers or certain employers keeps its position, so it can come first even if you don't qualify. The card says so; check first.

inputs.title: How what you enter is used
inputs.intro: We only ask for what we can use. Here's what each answer does.
inputs.privacy: All of this is calculated on your own device. None of it is sent or stored on a server, and lenders receive nothing.

purpose.name: Purpose
purpose.use: Remove instalment loans tied to other goods. Cash loans work for any purpose. Also picks the guidance you see.

amount.name: Amount
amount.use: Compare with the product's limits, and calculate the cost. Fixed fees weigh more on small loans.

term.name: Term
term.use: Compare with the product's limits, and calculate the cost. Some lenders set rates by term.

urgency.name: When you need it
urgency.use: Only to show a scam warning if you're in a hurry, as people in a hurry are easier to deceive.

income.name: Income
income.use: Compare with the product's minimum income, and work out your debt payments against the {limit} guideline.
income.order: Yes: changes the list and the affordability group

debt.name: Monthly debt payments
debt.use: Added to the new payment to work out your debt payment ratio.

age.name: Age
age.use: Compare with the product's age limits. Some lenders check your age when the contract ends.

proof.name: Proof of income
proof.use: Only applies if you choose "Salary paid in cash" or "No proof yet": loans listing income or salary papers come after others in their affordability group, with a note. The other choices change nothing. Loans whose documents are unknown aren't moved down.
proof.order: Yes, but only with those two choices

formula.title: How the real rate is calculated
formula.body: Every loan is turned into the same measure, based on your real cash flows:
formula.received: Money received at the start = amount borrowed − fees and insurance deducted from the payout − amounts paid upfront.
formula.payments: Monthly payment = scheduled principal and interest + monthly fees. Fees added to the loan raise the principal you repay.
formula.irr: The monthly rate (r) is the rate at which the money you receive equals today's value of everything you pay later. Specialists call it the IRR.
formula.apr: Real yearly rate = r × 12. This is the number used for ranking, directly comparable with reducing-balance rates lenders publish.
formula.effective: Rate including interest on interest = (1 + r)^12 − 1, shown in each loan's details.
formula.total: Total cost = everything you pay − money you actually receive. Late-payment penalties aren't included; they're shown as a separate warning.
formula.example: An illustration, not any lender's product: borrow {amount} over 24 months at a flat 1.5% a month, with a {fee} fee deducted from the payout. You receive {received}, repay {total} in total, cost {cost}, real rate {apr} a year.

sources.title: Where the figures come from
sources.intro: {ranked} of {total} products are ranked. The newest figures were checked on {date}. Each rate names its source and date:
sources.official: The lender's own pages and documents, including articles and app descriptions: {count} products. This includes company-wide rate frameworks, costed at their top.
sources.lender_partner: The lender's distribution partners: {count} products. They may be paid for referring loans.
sources.aggregator: Rate comparison sites: {count} products. They may be old or wrong, and often don't say how interest is calculated.
sources.press: The press: {count} products. They may be old.
sources.licensed: Wherever a figure comes from, only lenders on the State Bank of Vietnam's lists are listed.

assumptions.title: Our assumptions
assumptions.basisBank: When the source doesn't say how interest is calculated and the lender is a bank, we use reducing balance, which banks usually use.
assumptions.basisFinance: When the source doesn't say and the lender is a finance company, we use flat rate, the costlier reading, unless the lender's other documents say otherwise.
assumptions.top: With only a company-wide range, or a minimum that doesn't match the lender's own adverts, we only calculate at the top.
assumptions.promo: A 0% rate usually applies only to certain goods, so we don't use it for your cost.
assumptions.general: Some figures are about the lender in general, not that product. The card says so.
assumptions.fees: For now we only count mandatory insurance and monthly fees with a known amount. One-off fees such as application or commitment fees, and insurance that's optional or may not be mandatory, aren't counted, so the real cost could be higher. The card says so.

notUsed.title: What doesn't affect the ranking
notUsed.money: Money. No lender pays to rank higher. Vay Đúng takes no commission and doesn't sell your information. Our data has no field for it.
notUsed.approval: Your chance of approval. We don't know what a lender will decide. Ranking higher doesn't mean easier approval.

limits.title: Limits
limits.rate: The rate you're given is the lender's decision. Some ranges are very wide, so calculated figures are only estimates.
limits.secondary: Figures from comparison sites and the press may be old or wrong. When checking, we found figures that aren't in the lender's own documents. A product that looks cheap on such a figure may not really be cheap.
limits.fees: Many lenders don't publish all their fees and insurance.
limits.personal: We don't see your credit history, so we don't know whether you qualify.
limits.stale: This site is kept as an archive, so loans not re-checked for over 90 days are still ranked, but the results page then shows a notice with the oldest collection date. That is the date we read the source, not the date it was published, so check the date on each card.
limits.comparable: A company-wide range is often a ceiling, above what many people actually pay, while comparison sites may list only typical rates. So a lower-ranked loan isn't necessarily dearer, and a higher-ranked one isn't necessarily cheaper.

Data.title: The data used for ranking
Data.intro: {total} products from {lenders} lenders. {ranked} are ranked, and {secondary} use a rate that isn't from the lender's documents. Newest check: {date}.
